title: In a double complex with exact rows a zig-zag whose end is a boundary of the row-cokernel complex is trivial
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $A=(A_{p,q},d,\delta)_{p,q\ge0}$ be a homological double complex of $R$-modules: $R$-modules $A_{p,q}$ ($p,q\ge0$) and $R$-linear maps $d_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p-1,q}$ ($p\ge1$) and $\delta_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to A_{p,q-1}$ ($q\ge1$) with $d_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=0$, $\delta_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}=0$ and $\delta_{p-1,q}\circ d_{p,q}=d_{p,q-1}\circ\delta_{p,q}$ whenever defined; put $A_{p,q}=0$ if $p<0$ or $q<0$ and let $d_{0,q}$, $\delta_{p,0}$ and all maps out of or into a zero module be $0$. A morphism $\Phi:A\to B$ of such double complexes is a family of $R$-linear maps $\Phi_{p,q}:A_{p,q}\to B_{p,q}$ with $\Phi d=d\Phi$ and $\Phi\delta=\delta\Phi$. Let $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q=\operatorname{Coker}(d_{1,q}:A_{1,q}\to A_{0,q})$ with projection $\pi_q:A_{0,q}\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q$ ($q\ge0$); since $\delta_{0,q}(\operatorname{im}d_{1,q})=d_{1,q-1}(\delta_{1,q}(A_{1,q}))\subseteq\operatorname{im}d_{1,q-1}$, the map $\delta_{0,q}$ induces $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q:A^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{q-1}$ with $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_{q-1}\delta_{0,q}$ ($q\ge1$), and $A^{\mathrm{rt}}_\bullet$ is a chain complex of $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]; a morphism $\Phi$ induces the morphism of complexes $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}$ with $\Phi^{\mathrm{rt}}_q\pi_q=\pi_q\Phi_{0,q}$. Assume that every row of $A$ is exact in positive degrees: for all $q\ge0$ and $p\ge1$ the sequence $A_{p+1,q}\xrightarrow{d_{p+1,q}}A_{p,q}\xrightarrow{d_{p,q}}A_{p-1,q}$ is exact at $A_{p,q}$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Let $Z_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}A_{p,q}$ and $B_n(A)\subseteq T_n(A)$ be the modules of zig-zags and of trivial zig-zags of total degree $n$ [def-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module]. Let $n\ge0$ and $a\in Z_n(A)$, and suppose that $\pi_n(a_{0,n})$ lies in the image of $\delta^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}:A^{\mathrm{rt}}_{n+1}\to A^{\mathrm{rt}}_n$. Then $a\in B_n(A)$.

proof.text: Choose c in A_(0,n+1) representing an element y of the row-cokernel module A^rt_(n+1) whose image under delta^rt_(n+1) is pi_n(a_(0,n)). Since delta^rt_(n+1) pi_(n+1) equals pi_n delta_(0,n+1), the difference a_(0,n) minus delta_(0,n+1)(c) lies in the image of d_(1,n); choose e in A_(1,n) with d_(1,n)(e) plus delta_(0,n+1)(c) equal to a_(0,n). Let b in T_(n+1)(A) have only b_(1,n)=e and b_(0,n+1)=c nonzero. Then D_(n+1)(b)_(0,n)=a_(0,n), so replacing a by a-D_(n+1)(b) gives a zig-zag representing the same class and having zeroth component 0. This replacement is legitimate because B_n(A) is contained in Z_n(A) by [lem-weil-pbc-double-complex-zigzag-module-functorial].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M1 (lemma-no-spectral-sequence), proof, lines 18488-18496 (boundary lift and modification to arrange a_{0,i}=0)

proof.text: After the first step, suppose inductively that, after subtracting elements of B_n(A), the zig-zag a' has a'_(p,q)=0 for all p<k, where 1 <= k <= n and q=n-p. The zig-zag equation at (k,n-k), together with the already-zero component at (k-1,n-k+1), gives d_(k,n-k)(a'_(k,n-k))=0. Row exactness at A_(k,n-k) therefore supplies f in A_(k+1,n-k) with d_(k+1,n-k)(f)=a'_(k,n-k). Subtract the trivial zig-zag D_(n+1)(b) where b has only b_(k+1,n-k)=f nonzero; its (k,n-k) component is a'_(k,n-k), so the k-th component is killed while only the next component may change. Repeating for k=1,...,n produces a representative with every component zero. Thus the original zig-zag belongs to B_n(A).
